reviews.fact_before: if a neutral atom loses an electron then an atom with a negative charge will be formed
reviews.correction: Removing one electron from a neutral atom leaves a positive ion with charge +1, called a cation. Gaining an electron instead produces a negative ion. The original premise reverses the sign.
reviews.reason: The source gives the wrong charge and propagates it into several answers.

reviews.correction: An ion has a nonzero net electric charge; it is not a neutral atom. It may be a charged atom or a charged group of atoms.
reviews.reason: The source contradicts the definition of an ion.

reviews.fact_before: if two balanced forces act on an object in opposite directions then that object will remain stationary
reviews.correction: Zero net external force means constant velocity in an inertial frame. An object initially at rest stays at rest, while an object already moving can continue at constant speed in a straight line. Balanced forces do not prove that an object is stationary.
reviews.reason: The initial motion and other external forces are omitted. The original stationary conclusion is not established.

reviews.fact_before: if gas is heated then that gas will expand
reviews.correction: For a fixed amount of ideal gas at constant pressure, raising the kelvin temperature increases its volume. In a rigid sealed container, volume stays fixed and heating instead raises pressure. Heating does not always imply expansion.
reviews.reason: The gas law requires fixed amount and specified pressure or volume constraints.

reviews.fact_before: An increase in temperature causes a gas to expand.
reviews.correction: For a fixed amount of ideal gas at constant pressure, raising the kelvin temperature increases its volume. In a rigid sealed container, volume stays fixed and heating instead raises pressure. Heating does not always imply expansion.
reviews.reason: The gas law requires fixed amount and specified pressure or volume constraints.

reviews.fact_before: If a material is heated, it expands and the density decreases.
reviews.correction: A decrease in density follows an increase in volume only when mass remains fixed. Heating does not guarantee expansion: gas in a rigid sealed container keeps the same volume and mass while its pressure rises.
reviews.reason: The source turns a conditional expansion model into a universal material law.

reviews.fact_before: All times are measured in seconds.
reviews.correction: The second is the SI unit of time interval. Time intervals may also be expressed in minutes, hours, days, and other appropriate units. A particular instrument must be checked for its actual scale and resolution.
reviews.reason: An SI base unit is not the only unit used to measure time.

reviews.fact_before: All temperatures are measures of heat energy.
reviews.correction: Temperature is not the total energy of an object and is not a quantity of heat. Heat denotes energy transfer due to a temperature difference; internal energy also depends on the amount and properties of matter.
reviews.reason: The source equates distinct physical quantities and can misstate phase changes.

reviews.fact_before: Heat is present in all matter.
reviews.correction: A body has internal energy. Heat is energy transferred because of a temperature difference, not a substance or a stored amount present in every object.
reviews.reason: Stored internal energy and energy transfer are conflated.

reviews.fact_before: Heat energy is the amount of energy in a substance.
reviews.correction: A body has internal energy. Heat is energy transferred because of a temperature difference, not a substance or a stored amount present in every object.
reviews.reason: Stored internal energy and energy transfer are conflated.

reviews.fact_before: Liquids are always measured accurately by volume.
reviews.correction: Liquid volume can be measured with suitable graduated equipment, but the result has measurement uncertainty. Accuracy depends on calibration, scale resolution, and reading technique; using volume units alone does not ensure an accurate result.
reviews.reason: The universal accuracy claim ignores measurement uncertainty.

reviews.fact_before: All substances are composed of molecules.
reviews.correction: Not every substance consists of discrete molecules. Solid sodium chloride, for example, is an extended arrangement of sodium and chloride ions. Distinguish atoms, molecules, and ionic structures when describing matter.
reviews.reason: A molecular description has been applied to every kind of substance.

reviews.fact_before: All matter is made of molecules.
reviews.correction: Not every substance consists of discrete molecules. Solid sodium chloride, for example, is an extended arrangement of sodium and chloride ions. Distinguish atoms, molecules, and ionic structures when describing matter.
reviews.reason: A molecular description has been applied to every kind of substance.

reviews.fact_before: All rockets generate thrust by igniting an mixture of fuel and 'oxidiser'.
reviews.correction: Many chemical rockets burn fuel with an oxidizer, but this is not the only way to produce rocket thrust. An ion thruster uses electrical energy to accelerate expelled ions.
reviews.reason: The premise excludes demonstrated electric propulsion.

reviews.correction: Water is one chemical substance, not the name for all liquids. Ethanol is a different substance that is also liquid under ordinary room conditions. Liquid describes a state of matter, not a single chemical identity.
reviews.reason: The premise confuses a specific substance with a phase of matter.

reviews.fact_before: Ultimately, all energy on the earth comes from the sun.
reviews.correction: Sunlight is a major energy input to Earth, but not every energy source on Earth comes from the Sun. Natural radioactive decay contributes to geothermal energy inside Earth.
reviews.reason: The universal solar-origin claim excludes an independent energy source.

reviews.fact_before: Natural magnets are permanent magnets that never lose their magnetism.
reviews.correction: Permanent does not mean indestructible magnetization. Heating or mechanical shock can reduce a magnet's magnetization; sufficiently high temperature destroys ferromagnetic order.
reviews.reason: The source incorrectly claims permanent magnets can never lose magnetism.

reviews.fact_before: All objects, even wooden tables, are made up of molecules which vibrate to create their mass.
reviews.correction: Molecular vibrations are part of microscopic motion, but do not create the ordinary mass of a wooden table. Its mass is largely associated with atomic nuclei; most proton and neutron mass comes from the energy of their quarks and gluons.
reviews.reason: The source supplies a false origin of mass and an unrelated premise for sanding wood.
